terms.meaning: A written rule set that data must match before the app accepts it.
A library the app uses to check that data has the right shape.
Code that reads one outside data source and turns its records into the app's format.
A label saying how trusted and how timely a data source is.
The detailed content of one record, such as runs or a wicket flag.
A type that TypeScript builds automatically from a schema.

sections.name: File setup, SPORTS, SportSlug
sections.title: Imports and the list of sports
sections.what: Brings in the validation library and the allowed source classes, then lists the five sports the app handles: cricket, basketball, football, F1 and tennis.
sections.why: Keeping the sport list in one fixed place means a typo in a sport name is caught by the type checker.
sections.watch_out: Adding a sport here does not add its data or models anywhere else.

sections.name: incidentInput, IncidentInput
sections.title: Rules every incoming incident must meet
sections.what: Defines the required fields for one incident as an adapter produces it, and the type derived from them. Records that miss a field or have a bad value are rejected before storage.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its comment, which says this is the adapter output before storage.
sections.watch_out: Time fields are converted from text, so the exact formats accepted depend on how the date parsing works.

summary: Defines the sports the app knows about and the exact shape an incident must have, and checks incoming incident data against that shape.
purpose: Acts as the gatekeeper for incident records before they are stored, so records with missing or wrong fields are rejected.
why: Likely reason: data arrives from several source adapters, so one shared check keeps them consistent.
how: 1. Lists the five sports. 2. Builds a schema that each incident must satisfy: whole, non-negative numbers, text length limits, a source class from the allowed list, required source and rights ids, times turned into dates, and optional fields with defaults. 3. Exposes the type inferred from that schema.
inputs: Raw incident objects produced by source adapters.
outputs: Validated incident objects with defaults filled in, or validation errors.
risks: The payload is accepted as any key-value object, so its contents are not checked here. Changing the sport list affects every place that uses it.
debug: If a record is rejected, read the first validation error, which names the field. Check that the source class is one from the sources types file. Check that time fields are valid dates.
